Officers knew he was wanted for Firearms Smuggling and Burglary of a Building at which time they attempted a traffic stop. He refused to stop and a pursuit initiated in the 400 block of S. Douglas. The pursuit continued southbound and ended in the 400 block of Edwards. He exited his vehicle and ran northbound in-between houses. A perimeter was set up and he was ultimately located hiding in a dumpster in the alley of the 400 block of Dallas. Once he was located he fired multiple rounds at officers in which an Deputy with the Howard County Sheriff’s Office returned fire striking him in the hand. He was taken into Custody a short time later and taken to Hospital and Treated for his injuries.

Benavides stated he was awaken at approximately 0400 hours to the sound of rapid gunfire coming from the rear of a neighbors property which gave him a concern for safety for his family. Benavides stated a second burst of rapid gunfire occurred again sometime between 0405 and 0410 hours at which time he heard bullet fragments striking his residence. Believing that a drive by shooting might be occurring, Benavides went downstairs, exited the sliding rear door of his residence and stepped outside. It was at this time as he was stepping back inside he observed a subject jumping over the fence into his yard wearing a gray hoodie, ski mask, and black pants. Benavides stated he felt threaten, and retrieved his firearm from the kitchen table. Benavides stated he observed the subject walking toward him and fearing for his life, fired three rounds as the subject was approaching. The suspect then retreated to the fence where he came from. Benavides called 911.

incident_result_of: Emergency Call or Request for Assistance; Hostage/Barricade/Other Emerg Situation Specify type of call: Uniformed Patrol Officers were dispatched to 1907 Lamar Avenue in reference to a stabbing. Upon arrival, Officers found a female victim outside the motel with chest wounds. Officers learned the suspect in the stabbing was the husband of the victim, and he was inside the motel room with the victim’s children. Officers established a perimeter near the front door of the motel room entrance to begin verbal negotiation with the suspect. The suspect extended his arm out a window of the motel room holding a black handgun and pointed it at the officers, which resulted in the officers to retreat to cover behind parked vehicles. After officers obtained cover the suspected exited and re-entered the motel room holding a gun while taunting officers to shoot him. The armed suspect ultimately exited the motel room and walked hurriedly in the direction of officers pointing the gun at them, which resulted in officers to discharge their weapons striking the suspect once.

Main Street to investigate a report of a suspicious male who had been in a dressing room for over 30 minutes and would not respond to store employees who were preparing to close the store for the evening. The Officer eventually persuaded suspect to exit the dressing room. As the Officer attempted to detain suspect for further investigation, he broke away and ran toward the store’s main exit. The officer pursued and temporarily subdued suspect. As the Officer re-attempted to restrain suspect, he actively resisted arrest, and during a physical struggle with the Officer, suspect gained possession of the Officer’s taser. Suspect then ran a short distance inside the store before turning and pointing the taser at the officer placing the officer in immediate danger of being incapacitated. The officer properly reacted, firing hitting Suspect in the upper torso.

incident_result_of: Other Specify type of call: On August 10, 2024, a UTPD officer, while on duty, was contacted by a suicidal individual. This suicidal individual was known to the officer and purported to be in a house with a 7-month-old infant. The officer informed a UTPD supervisor and requested a welfare check from the Travis County Sheriff’s Office (TCSO) while en route to the scene. The officer arrived before other law enforcement and knocked on the door. The suicidal individual pointed a rifle at the officer and demanded she remove her ballistic vest. During the officer’s attempt to locate the infant and calm the suspect, an altercation ensued where the officer acted in self-defense, and the individual was shot, causing a non-life-threatening injury. The individual was later charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

civ_weapon: Carried, exhibited, or used a deadly weapon
incident_result_of: Other Specify type of call: Officers discharged their police weapons at the subject who was operating a wheeled front-end loader (weighing 28,193 lbs.) in a reckless and unsafe manner in the immediate area of moving vehicles and pedestrians in the parking lot of a concert venue as the event had ended. The subject used the heavy equipment to ram two police vehicles and had driven the front-end loader onto the eastbound lanes of the 11,000 block of Texas State Highway 191, traveling in a western direction – towards oncoming traffic. The officers discharged their weapons as well as other officers from another responding agency. The subject was wounded, taken into custody and transported to a local hospital where he recovered from his injuries and was subsequently transferred to a detention facility. The subject was charged with Aggravated Assault of a Peace Officer.
